places.place_id: monument to the great fire of london
places.now: still standing; the Monument, at the junction of Monument Street and Fish Street Hill
places.reason: Wren and Hooke's column (1671-77) is a well-documented landmark that stands where it did in Dickens's day.

places.now: Mount Etna, active volcano in Sicily
places.reason: A real, famous volcano; the gazetteer match is correct.

places.now: Mount Pleasant, Clerkenwell; Royal Mail sorting office on the site of the old Coldbath Fields prison
places.reason: Mount Pleasant is a well-known rising ground in Clerkenwell, and the gazetteer match is the right place.

places.now: timber-framed house on St Dunstan's Street, Canterbury, traditionally identified as Wickfield's house
places.reason: Wickfield's house is fictional; the coordinates are the traditional identification with a house in St Dunstan's Street, Canterbury, so the exact spot is uncertain.

places.now: Niger River, West Africa; the coordinates are its confluence with the Benue at Lokoja
places.reason: The river is real, but Dickens only says 'left bank of the Niger' for Jellyby's fictional Borrioboola-Gha, so no exact spot exists.

places.now: The Nore sandbank and anchorage at the Thames/Medway mouth, marked by the Nore buoy; the old lightship has gone
places.reason: The Nore was a well-known anchorage and sandbank off Sheerness, but the buoy or lightship position is approximate.

places.now: Millbank riverside, Westminster, north bank of the Thames
places.reason: This is a generic reference to the Middlesex shore leading toward Millbank, so the point is only a general riverside area near Millbank.

places.now: Northern England, a region with no precise point
places.reason: A broad region rather than a place; the coordinates are only a rough centroid and the gazetteer's Guiseley match is wrong.

places.now: Hoo/Cooling marshes of north Kent; no identifiable battery
places.reason: The Battery in Great Expectations is fictional and set in the Cooling/Hoo marshes, so the coordinates are only the village of Cooling.

places.now: Market Place, off Great Titchfield Street, Fitzrovia; the market is long gone
places.reason: Oxford Market stood just north of Oxford Street around today's Market Place, and the gazetteer's pub match is on that street, but the exact market footprint is uncertain.

places.now: Whitehall/Scotland Yard area; the Palace Court was abolished in 1849 and nothing of it survives
places.reason: The Palace Court was the Court of the Marshalsea of the Household, sitting near Whitehall; the location is approximate and the Preston match is wrong.

places.now: Pool of London, Thames near Tower Bridge; the working port has moved downriver
places.reason: The Port of London covered the whole tidal Thames, and the point given is the historic Pool of London at its heart.

places.now: unknown; probably fictional
places.reason: The Princess's Arms and Princess's Place in Dombey and Son appear to be fictional, with no firmly identified real counterpart.

places.now: Giza pyramid complex, near Cairo, Egypt
places.reason: The Great Pyramids of Giza are a famous, precisely known site.

places.now: Richmond Green, Richmond, London Borough of Richmond upon Thames (then in Surrey)
places.reason: Richmond Green is a well-documented open space, the setting for Estella's house in Great Expectations.

places.now: King's College London's Maughan Library and the Weston Street/Chancery Lane Rolls Estate area; Rolls Yard buildings demolished
places.reason: Rolls Yard was by the Rolls Chapel and Rolls House off Chancery Lane, now on the site of the Maughan Library, but its exact spot is uncertain.

places.now: Campagna Romana, the countryside around Rome, now largely suburban
places.reason: A real region around Rome, so the coordinates are a central point in the countryside southeast of the city.

places.now: Royal Military Academy Sandhurst; the Old College is still in use
places.reason: The Royal Military College was established at Sandhurst in 1812 and the Old College is still there.

places.now: fictional; no identifiable inn
places.reason: The Ship inn in Great Expectations is a fictional riverside or marshland inn with no real counterpart.

places.now: The Grapes, Narrow Street, Limehouse, still a pub, traditionally cited as the model
places.reason: The Six Jolly Fellowship Porters is fictional, and The Grapes on the Limehouse riverside is the usual candidate for its original.

places.place_id: sluice house on the kent marshes
places.now: fictional; no identifiable sluice-house
places.reason: The sluice-house in Great Expectations is a fictional structure on the Thames estuary marshes.

places.now: demolished; the area near City Road and Old Street, Finsbury
places.reason: St Luke's parish workhouse stood in the City Road/Old Street area of St Luke's, but I am unsure of the exact spot.

places.now: St Peter's Basilica, Vatican City
places.reason: A world-famous building at a well-known location.

places.now: Staple Inn, High Holborn, with its Tudor timber-framed front; the gazetteer match is correct
places.reason: Staple Inn is a surviving, well-documented former Inn of Chancery on High Holborn, so the gazetteer's guess is right.

places.now: Tottenham Court Road, running from St Giles to Euston Road
places.reason: A major, long-established London street; the coordinates are a midpoint along its length.
